source.title: Cefazolin in Chronic Hemodialysis Patients: A Safe, Effective Alternative to Vancomycin

atoms.canonical_statement: The study examined whether cefazolin could replace vancomycin for empiric treatment in a freestanding outpatient hemodialysis population and evaluated postdialysis cefazolin pharmacokinetics in anuric patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the role that cefazolin might have as an empiric antibiotic

atoms.canonical_statement: The microbiology review covered a freestanding outpatient hemodialysis center with a census of 217 patients over 7 months.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a census of 217 patients were examined during a 7-month period

atoms.canonical_statement: All non-urine cultures were categorized by source and Gram stain and tested for sensitivity to cefazolin, vancomycin, cefazolin plus gentamicin, and vancomycin plus gentamicin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All non-urine cultures were categorized by location

atoms.canonical_statement: Urine cultures were excluded from the microbiology analysis because urinary infections were rarely treated with parenteral antibiotics in this setting.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: urine cultures were excluded from further analysis

atoms.canonical_statement: The investigators did not determine whether positive cultures represented clinical infection, colonization, or contamination.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: No determination was made as to whether positive cultures represented true clinical infection, colonization, or contamination.

atoms.canonical_statement: A wound-culture subset labeled probable pathogens excluded yeast, selected low-pathogenicity gram-negative organisms, Corynebacterium species, and Staphylococcus epidermidis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a subset of wound cultures excluding nonpathogenic organisms was developed

atoms.canonical_statement: Selected anuric chronic hemodialysis patients with cefazolin-susceptible clinical infections received cefazolin intravenously over 5 minutes after dialysis, 1 g for 11 doses and 2 g for 4 doses.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cefazolin was administered as a 1-g (n = 11) or 2-g (n = 4) dose

population.label: Selected anuric chronic hemodialysis patients with cefazolin-susceptible infection

atoms.canonical_statement: Dialysis during the pharmacokinetic study used an F80 polysulfone dialyzer, while blood flow, dialysate flow, treatment time, and other prescription elements followed clinical need.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Dialysis was performed using an F80 polysulfone dialyzer.

atoms.canonical_statement: Cefazolin sampling included 15 pre-dose and 1-hour post-dose pairs, 15 pre- and postdialysis pairs, and 9 interdialysis peak-to-predialysis intervals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cefazolin levels were obtained before and 1 hour after 15 individual doses

atoms.canonical_statement: The investigators calculated volume of distribution, nondialysis and dialysis elimination rate constants and half-lives, urea reduction ratio, and cefazolin reduction ratio with classical pharmacokinetic formulas.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Classical pharmacokinetic formulas were used to determine Ke and t1/2

atoms.canonical_statement: Culture sensitivity comparisons used chi-square tests, cefazolin and urea reduction analyses used linear regression and categorical chi-square testing, and P <= 0.05 defined statistical significance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: P <= 0.05 was required for statistical significance.

atoms.canonical_statement: For all positive non-urine cultures, reported in vitro coverage was 52% with cefazolin, 73% with vancomycin, 50% with cefazolin plus gentamicin, and 94% with vancomycin plus gentamicin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cefazolin 52%; vancomycin 73%; cefazolin+gentamicin 50%; vancomycin+gentamicin 94%; overall P=0.001; cefazolin vs vancomycin P<0.001; cefazolin+gentamicin vs vancomycin P=0.120 NS;

outcome.definition: Proportion of cultures susceptible to each tested regimen

atoms.canonical_statement: Nineteen of 225 cultures, 8%, were reported as methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: MRSA was present in 19 cultures (8%).

atoms.canonical_statement: Among 47 gram-negative wound cultures, cefazolin covered 17, 36%, whereas vancomycin would have missed all 47.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Vancomycin would have missed all 47 of the gram-negative cultures, while cefazolin alone would have covered 17 (36%).

atoms.canonical_statement: Adding gentamicin to cefazolin extended gram-positive coverage to 7 of 18 MRSA cultures, 16 of 44 Staphylococcus epidermidis cultures, and 11 of 11 enterococcus cultures.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: seven of 18 MRSAs, 16 of 44 Staphylococcus epidermidis cultures, 11 of 11 enterococcus cultures

atoms.canonical_statement: In the 15-observation volume-of-distribution analysis, cefazolin volume of distribution averaged 0.126 L/kg with SD 0.047 and ranged from 0.070 to 0.182 L/kg.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Volume of distribution of cefazolin averaged 0.126 ± 0.047 L/kg

concept.text: cefazolin volume of distribution per kilogram

quantitative_result.effect_measure: mean volume of distribution per kilogram

atoms.canonical_statement: Absolute cefazolin volume of distribution averaged 8.97 L with SD 3.86 in the 15-observation analysis.
Peak cefazolin concentrations ranged from 79 to 452 micrograms/mL, with a mean of 193 micrograms/mL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Peak cefazolin levels ranged from 79 to 452 µg/mL (mean, 193 µg/mL).

atoms.canonical_statement: Nondialysis cefazolin elimination in anuric patients had mean Ke 0.027 per hour with SD 0.005, based on 9 interdialysis periods.

population.label: Anuric patients in nondialysis clearance analysis

atoms.canonical_statement: Nondialysis cefazolin half-life averaged 26.4 hours with SD 5.5 in the 9-period analysis.

population.label: Anuric patients in nondialysis clearance analysis

atoms.canonical_statement: Observed predialysis cefazolin concentrations ranged from 8.9 to 176 micrograms/mL, with a mean of 78 micrograms/mL, across samples obtained 24, 48, or 72 hours after the preceding dose.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Predialysis, or trough, cefazolin levels ranged from 8.9 to 176 µg/mL (mean, 78 µg/mL).

quantitative_result.original_result_text: range 8.9 to 176 µg/mL; mean 78 µg/mL; sampled at 24 h n=1, 48 h n=6, 72 h n=2

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors stated that extrapolated cefazolin trough concentrations remained above 8 micrograms/mL at both 48 and 72 hours for every dose studied.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: all predialysis, or trough, cefazolin levels remained above 8 µg/mL

atoms.canonical_statement: Dialysis cefazolin elimination had mean Ke 0.254 per hour with SD 0.109 across 15 dialysis observations.
Dialysis cefazolin half-life averaged 3.19 hours with SD 1.21 across 15 dialysis observations.
Mean cefazolin concentration fell from 50 micrograms/mL predialysis to 25 micrograms/mL postdialysis; observed ranges were 14.8 to 139 and 7.1 to 81 micrograms/mL, respectively.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Predialysis levels ranged from 14.8 to 139, with a mean of 50 µg/mL. Postdialysis levels ranged from 7.1 to 81 µg/mL

concept.text: serum cefazolin concentration before and after dialysis

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Predialysis range 14.8-139, mean 50 µg/mL; postdialysis range 7.1-81, mean 25 µg/mL

atoms.canonical_statement: Reported drug acquisition costs were $3.74 for cefazolin, $54.95 for vancomycin, $7.69 for cefazolin plus gentamicin, and $58.90 for vancomycin plus gentamicin.
Reported administration times were 5 minutes for cefazolin, 60 minutes for vancomycin, 35 minutes for cefazolin plus gentamicin, and 90 minutes for vancomycin plus gentamicin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 5 min 60 min 35 min 90 min

atoms.canonical_statement: All patients with clinical infections who were treated with cefazolin were reported to have clinical resolution of infection.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: All patients with clinical infections treated with cefazolin clinically resolved their infections.

atoms.canonical_statement: One cefazolin-treated patient developed a morbilliform rash that resolved after cefazolin was discontinued.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: One patient developed a morbilliform rash that resolved with discontinuation of cefazolin.

quantitative_result.original_result_text: One patient developed a morbilliform rash.

atoms.canonical_statement: For clinically stable outpatient hemodialysis patients in a setting with low MRSA prevalence, the authors considered cefazolin alone or with gentamicin a reasonable empiric choice until culture results were available.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: cefazolin alone or with gentamicin is a reasonable empiric antibiotic choice

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that vancomycin plus gentamicin offered the broadest empiric coverage, but cefazolin plus gentamicin provided nearly as broad coverage with lower cost and shorter administration time.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the combination of vancomycin plus gentamicin does provide the broadest empiric coverage

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors stated that empiric cefazolin may not be appropriate in hemodialysis populations with substantially higher MRSA rates than the study center.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Cefazolin may not be appropriate as empiric treatment in hemodialysis populations with significantly higher rates of MRSA infection.

atoms.canonical_statement: For cefazolin-susceptible infections in anuric patients dialyzed with polysulfone membranes, the authors recommended 1 g intravenously after each hemodialysis session.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: a 1-g intravenous dose after each hemodialysis session

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors suggested reducing the postdialysis cefazolin dose to 750 mg for patients weighing less than 50 kg to avoid potentially toxic peak concentrations.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: it may be prudent to give a 750-mg dose to patients weighing less than 50 kg

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that supplemental cefazolin doses between dialysis sessions were not needed when a sufficient 1-g postdialysis dose was used in anuric patients.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: supplemental nondialysis dosing is not needed with a sufficient (1-g) postdialysis dose

atoms.canonical_statement: The postdialysis dosing recommendation applied only to anuric patients; one excluded patient with residual urine output had substantially higher nondialysis clearance and low predialysis cefazolin levels.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The recommendation for postdialysis dosing is appropriate only for anuric hemodialysis patients.

atoms.canonical_statement: The pharmacokinetic study used only polysulfone dialyzers, and the effect of non-polysulfone membranes on cefazolin dose and frequency was unknown.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The current study was performed using only polysulfone dialyzers.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study did not measure cefazolin minimum inhibitory concentrations and instead interpreted concentrations against external susceptibility guidance.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the minimum inhibitory concentration of cefazolin was not measured in the current study

atoms.canonical_statement: No cefazolin-treated patient in the study cohort had bacteremia, so the paper did not directly test the postdialysis regimen as treatment for bacteremia during the study period.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: none of the study patients treated with cefazolin had bacteremia

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors estimated that replacing vancomycin would reduce drug acquisition costs by 93% with cefazolin alone and by 86% with cefazolin plus gentamicin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Drug acquisition costs would decrease by 93% if cefazolin was used alone or by 86% if used with gentamicin.

atoms.canonical_statement: The paper concluded that suspected infections in outpatient chronic hemodialysis settings with low MRSA rates could be treated empirically with cefazolin instead of vancomycin, while cefazolin-sensitive infections in anuric patients could receive postdialysis cefazolin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Suspected infections in chronic hemodialysis patients receiving treatment at outpatient facilities with low rates of MRSA infection
